subject: Post-call: Open vs proprietary model trade-offs + proposed eval action plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novafin.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: Open vs proprietary model trade-offs + proposed eval action plan

Hi Alyssa (and Tom),

Thanks again for a productive call earlier — appreciate you walking us through the Novafin risk-assist workflows and the dataset scope. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight action plan so we can get you a clear parity readout quickly: 

Key takeaways from call:
- Primary workload: customer-facing risk summaries + regulatory Q&A (short answers, < 150 tokens).
- Current proprietary baseline (ProdBase-v3) has strong factuality on internal docs but exhibits latency (~600ms P95) and is costly at scale.
- Main risks to you: hallucination on regulatory citations, semantic drift on short answers, and budget constraints for per-call costs.

Our recommended evaluation focus (short, 2-week exploratory sprint):
1) Models to trial (open candidates): Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama-2-13B-Chat (quantized 4-bit), and GPT-NeoX-20B trimmed variant.
2) Redwood baseline variants: ProdBase-v3 (your proprietary baseline) + Redwood-tuned-8B (our performant quantized candidate).
3) Acceptance gates (initial):
   - Factuality: reference-anchored hallucination rate <= 3% on a 500-query prompt bundle.
   - QA accuracy: Macro-F1 >= 0.88 on regulatory QA test set.
   - Latency: P95 generation latency <= 400ms on your typical prompt mix (short replies).
   - Cost: token-inference cost <= target (we’ll provide per-1K estimate once we pick the runtime).
4) Artefacts we’ll share: prompt bundle (v1) + benchmark instructions + evaluation notebook (Drive link below).

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline):
- Today/Tomorrow: I’ll upload the prompt bundle and benchmark playbook. (See attachments.)
- By EOD Wed: Redwood runs a baseline pass on 100 canonical queries to sanity-check hallucination vs ProdBase-v3.
- Week 1: Full automated batch across the 500-query bundle; provide per-model breakdowns (accuracy, hallucination, latency distribution, token cost estimates).
- Week 2: Joint readout + decision on which open model(s) to pilot in a limited canary.

Questions for you to confirm:
- Is the 500-query bundle representative? If you want to swap or add business-critical prompts, please send them by Tue EOD.
- Do you have any regulatory constraints we should include in the eval (e.g., must redact PII before model sees context)?

Links and artifacts (attached and Drive):
- prompt bundle: novafin_prompt_bundle_v1.zip (attached)
- benchmark instructions: novafin_benchmark_instructions_v1.pdf (attached)
- eval notebook: https://drive.google.com/novafin-eval-notebook
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/0937

If that plan looks good I’ll kick off the baseline pass tomorrow and loop in the infra team for runtime selection (we’ll test both hosted Redwood API and a dedicated quantized runtime to collect cost/latency trade-offs).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: novafin_prompt_bundle_v1.zip (zip, 12KB), novafin_benchmark_instructions_v1.pdf (pdf, 28KB)
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@novafin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Green <t.green@novafin.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Open vs proprietary model trade-offs + proposed eval action plan

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 500-query bundle sounds right; I’ll review the attached prompt bundle and send two priority prompt categories ("regulatory citations" and "customer-facing summaries") by Tue morning.
- For PII: yes, we need redaction pre-send for any customer identifiers; I’ll send the redaction checklist.
- On cost: our procurement wants a rough per-inference estimate for budgeting. If you can include cost buckets for hosted vs dedicated versus quantized on-prem, that’d be helpful.

Please proceed with the baseline pass and share early sanity results. We’re targeting a decision by Aug 6 for a pilot.

Thanks, Alyssa
Sr. Product Manager — Novafin
alyssa@novafin.com

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Open vs proprietary model trade-offs + proposed eval action plan

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the quick reply and the redaction note. Two quick updates: 

1) We started the sanity baseline pass this morning (100 canonical queries). Early signals: Redwood-tuned-8B has lower hallucination than open Mistral on citation tasks but slightly higher P95 latency vs the quantized Llama-2-13B in our hosted runtime. Full numbers by EOD Wed.

2) Cost buckets: I attached a preliminary delta table in the benchmark instructions PDF, but high-level: hosted-quantized runtimes are typically ~30-40% cheaper per-token vs non-quantized hosted; Dedicated reserved GPUs (Redwood Dedicated) push cost further down but require a commitment. We’ll produce per-1000-token estimates for the actual prompt mix once we complete the 500-query run.

Action items I’ll own:
- Deliver full baseline report (accuracy, hallucination, latency distribution, token cost est) by Wed EOD.
- Add a short section comparing open model trade-offs vs ProdBase-v3 on hallucination patterns and citation errors.

Karthik — can you confirm the exact runtime configurations you want us to capture (e.g., 8-bit quantized on c5-GPU-equivalent vs full fp16 on v100-class)? We want to capture both P95 latency and memory footprint for a possible dedicated-capacity recommendation.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Karthik — quick internal note to capture tasks and owners: 

- Marissa: run full 500-query pass, assemble report, and include the per-runtime cost table (owner: Marissa; due: 2027-07-21 EOD).
- Karthik: please profile these runtime configs and reply with recommended test matrix by EOD today: 
   a) hosted fp16 (standard host)
   b) hosted 4-bit quantized (int4)
   c) dedicated 8-bit quantized (reserved pool)
   d) dedicated fp16 (reserved pool)
   For each config specify expected P95, memory footprint, and any compatibility caveats.
- CS/Legal: prepare redaction checklist + simple NDA appendix for accessing sample user data (I’ll ping CS).

We should also prepare a short appendix for the Novafin readout that explains our parity criteria in plain language (factuality thresholds, gating metrics) so the procurement team can sign off. Marissa — happy to jump on a short prep call before Wed readout if useful.

Vivek
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
